title: HIST 2111 or HIST 2112 (Survey of U.S. History I)
description: A survey of United States history, either to or since the Civil War era. At public universities in some states, such a course also meets a legislative requirement in national and state history.
notes: Choice slot: Georgia Tech's HIST 2111 or HIST 2112. Official descriptions are in data/raw/gatech/ (courses-hist page).

title: APPH 1040 or APPH 1050 or APPH 1060 (Scientific Foundations of Health)
description: A short wellness course on the science of health, physical activity, or well-being and resilience, required of all undergraduates.
notes: Choice slot: Georgia Tech's APPH 1040, 1050, or 1060 (2 hours). Official descriptions are in data/raw/gatech/ (courses-apph page).

title: Social Science Elective (US Constitution)
description: A social science course on American government or the Constitution, such as political science or public policy, which also meets a state requirement on the US and state constitutions.
notes: Georgia Tech suggests POL 1101, INTA 1200, or PUBP 3000.

title: Lab Science
description: A laboratory science course such as physics, chemistry, biology, or earth science, with a lab component.
notes: Georgia Tech: three lab sciences; one must be PHYS 2211 and two in the same discipline.

title: Social Science Elective
description: A course in the social sciences, such as psychology, economics, sociology, or political science, chosen from an approved list.

title: CS 2050 or CS 2051 (Introduction to Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science)
description: A discrete mathematics course for computer science: logic, proofs, induction, sets, functions, relations, counting, and graphs, with an honors version.
notes: Choice slot: Georgia Tech's CS 2050 or CS 2051 (honors). Official descriptions are in data/raw/gatech/ (courses-cs page).

title: Ethics Course
description: A course on ethical, legal, and social issues in computing, such as privacy, intellectual property, professional responsibility, and the impact of technology on society.
notes: Georgia Tech: one of CS 3001, CS 4001, CS 4002, CS 4003, CS 4726, or SLS 3110.

title: Junior Design (Part 1)
description: The first half of a two-semester team design sequence: students form teams, gather requirements from a client, and design a substantial software system.
notes: Georgia Tech's two-semester Junior Design capstone; the plan doesn't list its course options.

title: Junior Design (Part 2)
description: The second half of a two-semester team design sequence: teams implement, test, and deliver the system designed in the first half and present their work.
notes: Georgia Tech's Junior Design capstone, second semester.

title: Humanities Elective
description: A course in the humanities, such as literature, philosophy, history, art, or languages, chosen from an approved list.

title: Thread Course
description: A computer science (or related) course required by, or chosen from, one of the student's two chosen specialization tracks ("Threads"), such as intelligence, systems and architecture, theory, or people.
notes: Georgia Tech: the degree combines two of eight Threads.

title: Probability & Statistics Option
description: A course in probability and statistics, such as probability theory, applied statistics, or engineering statistics.
notes: Georgia Tech: MATH 3215, MATH 3670, CEE/ISYE 3770, or ISYE 2027 and 2028.
